 Follow Heavy metal rock star dead at 61 — after revealing ‘medical issue’
 Audrey Rock Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:29 AM UTC 2 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Danzig guitarist John Christ has died at the age of 61.
 "Friends, It is with a heavy heart that we must inform you of the peaceful passing of John Christ on November 15, 2026," a statement posted to his official Instagram page Monday read.
 It also noted that services are not planned and "kindly" asked "everyone to respect the family's privacy during this time."
 The statement concluded, "John loved each and every one of you."
 Danzig guitarist John Christ, seen above in an undated photo, has died.
 No additional information, including a cause of death, was immediately shared following the announcement, though the iconic heavy metal guitarist had previously hinted at health issues.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "Hey y'all, JC here!" the rocker wrote via Instagram on Sept. 2. "I wanted to give my disciples an update on what has been happening because inquiring minds want to know."
 The performer — real name John Wolfgang Knoll — wrote that he'd "recently" been "focusing on a medical issue that [had] been kicking [his] butt," and noted that he was "in the process of recuperating."
 The musician, pictured above with pals in an Instagram upload, was 61. Instagram/@thejohnchrist
 The metal guitarist, pictured here in a throwback photo with Ozzy Osbourne, had previously hinted at health issues. Instagram/@thejohnchrist
 He added that doctors had suggested he "take a few months off to rest up" and to let his "body get back to normal." He also informed followers that he'd be "unable to do any lessons or gigs until further notice."
 He concluded, "I really appreciate all of your support over the years and especially now while I heal up. I will post up here as soon as that happens and things start rolling again. Rock on!"
 Advertisement Advertisement The musician added a postscript, which read, "If there's radio silence, it's not because JC doesn't love you, it's because I'm under doctor's orders."
 A rep for the late guitarist was not immediately available to Page Six for comment on Wednesday.
 The performer, seen in an undated photo, wrote in September that he was "under doctor's orders." Instagram/@thejohnchrist
 The Maryland-born rocker was a founding member of Danzig — which began with Glenn Danzig in New Jersey back in 1987 as the rock group Samhain.
 He was known for his blues-influenced performances, which helped define the band's distinctive style.
 The late musician left the band in 1995 and released his only solo album, "Flesh Caffeine," in 1999.
